US fashion council CEO Steven Kolb resigns after NYFW protest clash

Council of Fashion Designers of America (CDFA) chief executive Steven Kolb has stepped down following an altercation with animal rights activists during New York Fashion Week.

By Gracie Partington 21 September 2026

Comment
NEW YORK, NEW YORK - SEPTEMBER 13: A protester holds a sign as models walk the runway during the COS New York Fashion Week fashion show at 161 Water Street on September 13, 2026 in New York City. (Photo by Taylor Hill/Getty Images)
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 1:39
Instaread

Kolb was filmed physically restraining two protesters during the Cos catwalk show on 13 September, after activists from animal rights campaign group, People for the Ethical Treatment of Animals (PETA) disrupted the show to protest H&M Group-owned Cos’s use of wool.

Kolb was subsequently placed on leave by the CFDA on 14 September, pending a review of the incident. He had held the role of CEO  for 15 years and been with the organisation for more than two decades.

Kolb then stepped down permanently, the CFDA board of directors confirmed in a statement shared on Instagram on Saturday (19 September). It said: “Steven Kolb has been a dedicated leader and tireless champion of American fashion throughout his more than two decades at the CFDA.”

The board added that it “respects Steven’s decision to step down” and thanked him for his “many years of leadership and service” to the organisation and the wider fashion industry.

It said Kolb leaves the non-profit organisation “well positioned, with a clear mission and dedicated team, to carry out the important work ahead as we look to the future of American fashion.”

Advertisement

The CFDA has not yet announced a successor.
